answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and region-scoped during peak settlement; the objective is sustained availability without dropping customer writes. Rollback is ruled out by the non-revertible security patch (b1 is therefore inapplicable). Circuit breakers (b4) fail requests and risk losing writes. Read-replica routing (b5) previously relieved dashboard/read load, which does not match a write-heavy settlement path. That leaves regional failover (b2: prior clean shift and fast latency recovery) versus adding capacity (b3: headroom absorbed a peak, but was provisioned before the surge). I intend a small guarded failover as the best current fit to a primary-only degradation, while verifying b2 and b3 because archive details may not transfer to mid-peak writes and failover can perturb downstream settlement. Cause (release vs regional saturation vs mixed load) remains unproven.
